blocks.content: The polling topic ended with a real, honest cost, most polling requests find nothing new at all, genuinely wasted effort. Long polling is a genuine, clever improvement that reduces this waste significantly, using a small but meaningful change to how the server actually responds.

The idea is simple once you see it: instead of the server answering immediately every single time, whether or not anything is actually new, it waits, holding the request open until it genuinely has something worth reporting.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437778008-107860252.png
1. The Key Difference From Plain Polling
blocks.text: 1. The Key Difference From Plain Polling

blocks.content: Plain polling, exactly as covered in the previous topic, gets an immediate answer every single time, usually just no, nothing new. Long polling instead has the server deliberately WAIT to answer, holding the connection open until something actually happens, then finally responding right at that moment.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437778008-351805070.png
blocks.alt: The Key Difference From Plain Polling

blocks.content: 2. How Holding a Connection Open Actually Works
blocks.text: 2. How Holding a Connection Open Actually Works

blocks.content: When a long polling request arrives, the server does not respond right away. It deliberately keeps that connection open, genuinely waiting, without sending anything back yet. Only once real new data actually becomes available does the server finally send its response, right at that moment.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437778008-650390971.png
blocks.alt: How Holding a Connection Open Actually Works

blocks.content: 3. What Happens Right After a Response
blocks.text: 3. What Happens Right After a Response

blocks.content: The moment the server finally responds with new data, that specific request is complete. The client, having just received an update, immediately opens a brand new long poll request right away, ready to wait again for whatever happens next.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437778009-789924289.png
blocks.alt: What Happens Right After a Response

blocks.content: 4. Handling a Long Wait With Nothing Happening
blocks.text: 4. Handling a Long Wait With Nothing Happening

blocks.content: A held open connection cannot genuinely wait forever without eventually causing real problems. If a real, meaningful stretch of time passes with nothing new happening at all, the server eventually times out and responds anyway, typically with an empty result, and the client simply opens another long poll request right away to keep waiting.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437869258-192604996.png
blocks.alt: Handling a Long Wait With Nothing Happening

blocks.title: Why a timeout is genuinely necessary
blocks.content: Holding connections open indefinitely with absolutely no time limit at all would tie up real server resources unpredictably. A sensible timeout keeps this held open pattern practical and bounded, even during genuinely quiet periods with nothing happening.
5. The Real, Measurable Improvement

Compared to plain polling many quick, mostly empty round trips, long polling produces fewer round trips overall, and each one is genuinely more meaningful, since it only actually completes once there is real data to report, rather than firing on a fixed timer regardless of whether anything actually changed.

6. A Real World Analogy

Plain polling is like repeatedly walking up to the kitchen and asking, is my food ready yet, over and over. Long polling is like telling the waiter, please come find me the moment it is actually ready, and simply waiting, with the waiter reaching out proactively the instant there is genuinely something to report.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437869260-276648860.png

blocks.title: The waiter still has to physically come find you
blocks.content: Even in this improved analogy, the waiter still has to make a trip to reach you, exactly like long polling still requiring a new HTTP request to be opened right after each response. It is a real improvement, not a complete elimination of the underlying request cycle.
7. Still Built Entirely on Ordinary HTTP
blocks.text: 7. Still Built Entirely on Ordinary HTTP

blocks.content: Despite the improvement, long polling requires no new protocol at all, it is still built entirely on the exact same ordinary HTTP requests covered throughout the previous module, just with a deliberately different waiting pattern on the server side. This is exactly why it works reliably almost everywhere plain HTTP already works.
/engineering/library/cn/images/1785437869260-516841816.png
blocks.alt: Still Built Entirely on Ordinary HTTP

8. Common Mistakes and Key Takeaways

["Assuming long polling eliminates HTTP overhead entirely, when each individual response still requires opening a brand new request right afterward, just far less frequently than plain polling.","Forgetting that a sensible timeout is genuinely necessary, holding connections open with no limit at all would tie up real server resources unpredictably.","Long polling reduces wasted requests by having the server wait to respond until something genuinely new exists.","It is still built entirely on ordinary HTTP, requiring no new protocol at all.","A timeout with automatic reconnection keeps the pattern practical even during genuinely quiet periods."]
items: Assuming long polling eliminates HTTP overhead entirely, when each individual response still requires opening a brand new request right afterward, just far less frequently than plain polling.
Forgetting that a sensible timeout is genuinely necessary, holding connections open with no limit at all would tie up real server resources unpredictably.
Long polling reduces wasted requests by having the server wait to respond until something genuinely new exists.
It is still built entirely on ordinary HTTP, requiring no new protocol at all.
A timeout with automatic reconnection keeps the pattern practical even during genuinely quiet periods.
